explain.say: Have you ever looked at a blank page and thought, where do I start? Here is a trick: draw first, write after! Look at the plan on the board. We will plan a story about Diego and his dog.

faq.q: What goes in the first box?
faq.a: The start of your story: who is in it and where they are. A quick drawing is plenty.

faq.q: How do I end my story?
faq.a: Show how the problem gets fixed, or how the characters feel at the end. Happy, surprised or proud endings all work.
asks: How do I finish a story?

faq.q: How do I turn pictures into sentences?
faq.a: Look at one picture at a time and say what is happening out loud. Then write down what you said, starting with a capital letter.
asks: How do I write from my plan?

faq.q: Do my drawings need to be good?
faq.a: Not at all! Stick people and simple shapes are perfect. The drawing is just there to help you remember your ideas.
asks: I am not good at drawing

faq.a: Yes. A teacher or grown-up can talk through the boxes with you, or write your key words while you tell the story.

facts: A story usually has a beginning, a middle and an end.
Drawing a plan before writing is a common way to sort out ideas.

quiz.say: What goes in the middle box?
quiz.show: What goes in the middle box?
quiz.why: The middle shows what happens, often a problem.

wrong.1: The title goes at the top, not in the middle box.
wrong.2: Your name goes on the page, not in the story boxes.

quiz.say: What do you write under each picture?
quiz.why: One key word helps you remember the idea for that box.

wrong.1: A whole page is too much for a plan. Just one word.
wrong.2: One key word under each picture helps you later.
